content.title: About
content.content: Chives (Allium schoenoprasum) are a perennial herb from the onion family, cultivated for its aromatic green leaves. Raw chive stalks have a mild onion flavor with a slightly bitter note. They are commonly used as a fresh garnish in salads, sauces, soups, and as a topping for various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chives belong to the same genus as onions, garlic, and leeks.
Leaves can grow up to 15 cm long and form dense clumps.
The plant thrives in pots and windowsills, making it a popular indoor herb.
Only the green leaves are eaten; stems and roots are generally discarded.
Chives produce small purple flower clusters that are edible and often used as a decorative garnish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Chives provide a good amount of vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in chives supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Its low calorie content and dietary fiber help promote satiety and regular digestion.

items.title: Sulfur‑containing compounds
items.content: Compounds such as allicin give chives their characteristic aroma and may have antimicrobial properties.

items.title: Allergy to Allium
items.content: People allergic to onions, garlic, or other Allium species may react to chives.

items.title: Possible stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of raw chives can cause discomfort in individuals with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Microbial contamination
items.content: As with any fresh herb, chives can be contaminated with bacteria, so they should be washed thoroughly before use.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use chives fresh: sprinkle them over soups, omelets, potatoes, salads, sauces, and marinades. They can be finely chopped and mixed into butter or cottage cheese for a flavored spread. While they can be lightly sautéed, most of their flavor is released when eaten raw.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chives in the refrigerator wrapped in a slightly damp paper towel and placed inside a plastic bag. They stay fresh for 7–10 days. For longer storage, freeze the leaves in small bags, though some aroma may be lost.
